newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus opposition group rejects deal with Russia.
newsitem.headline: Belarus opposition group rejects deal with Russia.

text.p: Opposition leaders in Belarus said on Monday that they did not recognise a unification deal with Russia signed by President Alexander Lukashenko last week and predicted it would strengthen public support for the country's independence.

"The fuss around the charter has brought a steady strengthening of support for independence in Belarus," Lyavon Barshchevski, acting president of the opposition Popular Front, told a news conference in the Belarussian capital, Minsk.
The Popular Front, which acknowledges it has only minority support among the population of 10 million, has staged a series of protests in recent months against Lukashenko's authoritarian rule.
The demonstrations were often broken up roughly by police, who arrested dozens of protesters.

But a majority of Belarussians, who feel a close affinity with Russia and are nostalgic for the former Soviet Union, support the charter signed by Lukashenko and Russian President Boris Yeltsin in a glittering ceremony in the Kremlin on Friday.

Barshchevski said the charter threatened the independence won by Belarus when the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991 and he and other Popular Front leaders told the news conference that Russia had imperialist ambitions.
